en_excerpt: A personal trainer on staying strong after 30, building routines clients can truly keep, and why exercise is a commitment for life.
en_meta_description: Why strength training after 30 protects muscle and bone — and how to build an exercise routine you can genuinely keep for life.
en_content:
Text: Ana Paula, Personal Trainer

https://www.instagram.com/fitandstrongwithana/

As a woman over 30, I understand how difficult it is to fit a training routine into everyday life. However, I also know how essential it is, because from that age onwards we start to lose muscle mass more quickly, which has a direct impact on bone density. Weight training is the best tool to fight that process, and that is why I insist so much on building routines that my clients can genuinely keep in the long term — for life.

As a Personal Trainer, my mission is to help each client find the best exercise routine, aligned with their reality and their lifestyle, so that training is continuous and sustainable — and not something momentary. After all, physical exercise is a commitment for your whole life, not only a way to achieve the “summer body”.

My name is Ana Paula, I am a Personal Trainer with 5 years of experience in the field. I am passionate about movement and about helping, especially beginners, to take the first step into an exercise routine, also promoting a better relationship with exercise and food.

Over these five years of work, I have also taken vocational courses in the areas of Nutrition and Mat Pilates, because I believe that constant upskilling is essential. To really contribute to improving physical health, which is directly linked to mental health, it is essential to keep updating yourself and, above all, to listen to each client, respecting their history and their experiences.

Movement is medicine!

To age with health, independence and quality of life, we need to stay strong.
